newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia considers incentives for plantations.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia considers incentives for plantations.

text.p: Indonesia's Investment Minister, Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo, said on Tuesday the government might offer fiscal incentives for plantation firms in a bid to attract more investment in the agricultural sector.
"Considering the amount of investment in this sector which is still below expectation, further efforts are needed to make it more attractive for investors," Sanyoto told parliament.
"The efforts include the possibility of offering fiscal incentives," Sanyoto said.
He did not give details of the possible incentives but said certain agricultural products had shown encouraging developments and yielded positive results.
These included rubber, coconut, coffee and crude palm oil, Sanyoto said.
Indonesia is among the world's largest producers of rubber and crude palm oil.

Sanyoto said, however, domestic investment in the agricultural sector reached a total of 43.3 trillion rupiah until August 31, 1996, with an average growth of 345 percent in every five year development plan (Pelita) since 1969.
Foreign investment in the agricultural sector also rose an average of 508 percent every five years to reach a total of $2.8 billion in the same period, he said. $1=2,323 rupiah
